newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA CHAMPIONS DALIAN KICK OFF SEASON WITH WIN.
newsitem.headline: CHINA CHAMPIONS DALIAN KICK OFF SEASON WITH WIN.

text.p: Defending champions Dalian Wanda took a swift and decisive step towards their third title in four years on Sunday with victory in the first match of China's first division professional soccer league season.
Dalian Wanda, who won the league in 1994 and 1996, extended their unbeaten record to 35 matches after the Sunday's 2-0 victory against Vanguard Huandao 2-0 in the central city of Chongqing.
Dalian Wanda pulled ahead in the 34th minute when Wang Peng scored and raised the count to 2-0 when Xu Hui connected in the 54th minute in a quick counter-attack.
Vanguard Huandao, promoted from the second division after coming top last season, had their chances to score but failed to convert before a home crowd of 40,000.

Coached by German Klaus Schlappner, former head coach of the Chinese national squad, Vanguard Huandao have moved from Wuhan in central Hubei province to the soccer-crazy city of Chongqing, the Xinhua news agency said.
Schlappner said the result reflected the gap between the top teams in the first and second divisions.
Last season's runners-up Shanghai Shenhua proved too strong for visiting Yanbian Aodong, winning 2-0 at home.
Liu Jun opened the scoring in the third minute after heading home a cross from Fan Zhiyi, China's 1996 footballer of the year.
Fan scored a penalty in the 57th minute after Yanbian Aodong committed a foul in the box, ensuring the win for Shanghai Shenhua, who won the league title in 1995.
In southern Guangzhou, Guangzhou Apollo edged Guangdong Hongyuan 1-0 in a rain-soaked match.
In the day's other matches, Beijing Guo'an were forced to a goalless draw at home by Sichuan Quanxing.
August First defeated Tianjin Lifei, playing on their home turf, 1-0, and Jinan Taishan suffered a surprise 0-1 home loss to Qingdao Hainiu, the other team promoted from the second division.
